negative_findings.reason: Reviewed the store leg in `plugins/cartflows/admin-core/ajax/common-settings.php:50-60`, `plugins/cartflows/admin-core/ajax/common-settings.php:97-113`, and `plugins/cartflows/admin-core/ajax/common-settings.php:221-246`: only users who already have `cartflows_manage_settings` can register/reach the AJAX action, the handler re-checks that capability, verifies the `cartflows_save_global_settings` nonce, and entity-encodes `global_css`/`global_js` before `update_option`. The matching load leg is `Cartflows_Frontend::custom_script_option()` in `plugins/cartflows/classes/class-cartflows-frontend.php:507-595`, which reads `_cartflows_global_scripts` and deliberately decodes the saved CSS/JS into `<style>`/`<script>` blocks. `plugins/cartflows/admin-core/inc/admin-menu.php:339-348` shows `cartflows_manage_settings` is granted to administrators by default, and any broader delegation is an administrator-controlled role-manager choice in `plugins/cartflows/admin-core/ajax/common-settings.php:368-456`. REFUTATION ATTEMPT: I treated this as the strongest stored-XSS candidate because the read leg is intentionally raw script execution, but I could not prove an attacker-reachable write leg below admin or admin-delegated settings access.

negative_findings.area: Per-flow and per-step custom JS/CSS/script meta flows
negative_findings.reason: Reviewed the store legs in `plugins/cartflows/admin-core/ajax/steps.php:380-433` and `plugins/cartflows/admin-core/ajax/flows.php:121-165`. Both require `cartflows_manage_flows_steps` and dedicated nonces before calling `MetaOps::save_meta_fields()`. `plugins/cartflows/admin-core/inc/meta-ops.php:29-99` shows the shared saver applies `FILTER_SCRIPT` to script-bearing fields, and the relevant meta definitions map `wcf-custom-script`, `wcf-step-custom-js`, `wcf-step-custom-css`, `wcf-flow-custom-script`, `wcf-flow-custom-js`, and `wcf-flow-custom-css` to that filter in `plugins/cartflows/classes/class-cartflows-default-meta.php:299-309` and `plugins/cartflows/classes/class-cartflows-default-meta.php:433-442`. The load leg is again `plugins/cartflows/classes/class-cartflows-frontend.php:523-595`, which reads those meta keys and decodes them into frontend `<style>`/`<script>` sinks. `plugins/cartflows/admin-core/inc/admin-menu.php:339-348` grants `cartflows_manage_flows_steps` to administrators by default; `plugins/cartflows/admin-core/ajax/common-settings.php:379-385` shows any non-admin grant is an explicit role-manager setting. REFUTATION ATTEMPT: if I could reach either meta-save action as a low-privilege or unauthenticated actor, the raw frontend sink would support a stored-XSS claim, but I could not trace such a write path in default code.

Reviewed the product-meta store leg in `plugins/cartflows/modules/woo-dynamic-flow/classes/class-cartflows-wd-flow-product-meta.php:36-40` and `plugins/cartflows/modules/woo-dynamic-flow/classes/class-cartflows-wd-flow-product-meta.php:200-208`, where the value is only saved during the WooCommerce product-edit save hook and is normalized with `sanitize_text_field()` before storage. The matching load leg in `plugins/cartflows/modules/woo-dynamic-flow/classes/class-cartflows-wd-flow-product-actions.php:99-107` reads the stored meta and escapes it with `esc_html()` before replacing the button label. REFUTATION ATTEMPT: this is a classic stored-XSS pattern on paper, but the read leg escaping defeats executable output and I did not find an alternate unescaped sink for the same meta key.

negative_findings.area: Second-order SQLi coverage for stored option/meta values
negative_findings.reason: I specifically looked for `get_option()`/`get_post_meta()`/related stored-value reads being reused in later SQL sinks. Repository review of SQL call sites in files such as `plugins/cartflows/classes/class-cartflows-admin.php:533-545`, `plugins/cartflows/admin-core/ajax/meta-data.php:191-202`, `plugins/cartflows/modules/woo-dynamic-flow/classes/class-cartflows-wd-flow-product-meta.php:99-109`, and `plugins/cartflows/abilities/class-cartflows-ability-runtime.php:920-923` did not produce a traced option/meta -> raw SQL path. Where SQL exists, it is either prepared from fresh request data or operates on unrelated constants/runtime IDs, while nearby stored-value reads are used for control flow or later escaped output instead of query construction. REFUTATION ATTEMPT: I treated stored meta like flow IDs, checkout product arrays, and saved settings as potential second-order inputs, but I could not prove any of them are later interpolated into a SQL sink without preparation, so no second-order SQLi finding is justified.
